name: Beef burger
headline: One burger's beef needs about as much water as two months of daily showers, and warms the planet as much as driving a petrol car roughly 20 km.
why: Cattle burp methane and need a lot of feed and land. Beef emits more per gram of protein than any other common food.
Mostly rain and irrigation water for feed and pasture: around 15,400 litres per kilo of beef.
Fine occasionally. Eating red and processed meat often is linked to bowel cancer and heart disease.
Cattle ranching is the single largest driver of tropical deforestation, and pasture takes more land than any other human use.
Meatpacking is among the most dangerous factory jobs; ranching also supports many rural livelihoods.
stages: Leftovers|1|A wasted burger wastes all of the above
deps: Grassland and feed crops|About three-quarters of the world's farmland feeds livestock, for under a fifth of our calories.
A stable climate|Heat and drought cut pasture growth, so beef undermines its own supply.
alts: Bean or lentil burger|Roughly 90% less carbon, land and water for the same protein.|-1,-1.5,2,-0.5,0|EASY|150|60000
Chicken burger|About a sixth of the climate impact of beef.|-1.5,-2.5,0,-2,-1.5|EASY|110|35000
Beef as a treat, not a habit|Halving beef is the biggest single food change most people can make.|-2,-3,-0.5,-3.5,-1|MEDIUM|80|30000
qa: Is grass-fed beef better?|For animal welfare and local wildlife, often yes. For climate, usually not: grass-fed cattle grow slower, live longer and emit more methane per kilo, and need more land.
Why does a cow matter more than a car?|It doesn't on its own, but there are about 1.5 billion cattle. Livestock produce around 14.5% of human-caused greenhouse gases, similar to all transport.
src: FAO, Tackling Climate Change Through Livestock

name: Chicken
headline: Chicken has about a sixth of beef's climate impact, but the world now raises over 70 billion chickens a year, most in sheds they never leave.
why: Around 10 kg CO₂e per kilo, mostly from growing feed.
Around 4,300 litres per kilo, mostly for feed crops.
Lean protein. Routine antibiotic use on farms fuels drug-resistant infections.
Soy feed is linked to deforestation, and manure pollutes rivers near intensive farms.
Processing-line work is fast, low paid and injury-prone.
deps: Soy from South America|A large share of the world's soy becomes animal feed.
Working antibiotics|Farms use a large share of the world's antibiotics.
alts: Tofu, beans or chickpeas|A third of the carbon and far less land.|-1,-1.5,2,-0.5,0|EASY|40|15000
Higher-welfare or organic chicken|Fewer birds, more space, less routine medication.|-2,-2.5,1,-2,-0.5|EASY|0|0
qa: Is chicken the sustainable meat?|It is the lower-carbon meat. It is also the one with the most animals per meal and the most intensive farming, so it trades climate for welfare and local pollution.

name: Fish & seafood
unit: one serving of fish or seafood (150 g)
headline: More than a third of the world's fish stocks are now fished faster than they can breed, up from a tenth in the 1970s.
why: Ranges widely: small wild fish are low-carbon, farmed prawns and trawled fish are high.
Wild fish need almost no freshwater; farmed fish need it for feed and ponds.
Oily fish is one of the best sources of omega-3. Large predators like tuna carry mercury.
Overfishing, bycatch and bottom trawling damage ocean life; prawn farms have replaced mangroves.
Forced labour is well documented on distant-water fishing fleets.
deps: Healthy oceans|Fish stocks collapse when too few adults are left to breed.
Mangroves and seagrass|Nurseries for young fish, often cleared for farms.
alts: Mussels, sardines, mackerel|Low on the food chain: low carbon, abundant, and mussels clean the water they grow in.|-1,0,3,0.5,0|EASY|30|0
Certified sustainable fish|Look for MSC (wild) or ASC (farmed) labels.|-2,-1.5,2.5,-1.5,-0.5|EASY|0|0
qa: Is farmed fish better than wild?|It depends on the species. Farmed mussels and oysters are among the lowest-impact animal foods. Farmed salmon and prawns eat wild-caught fish and soy, and can pollute coastal water.
src: FAO, State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2024

name: Cup of coffee
unit: one cup of coffee with a splash of milk
headline: It took about 130 litres of water to grow the beans for this one cup: nearly a full bathtub.
why: Farming and roasting the beans, plus milk. A large latte can triple it because of the milk.
Coffee trees are thirsty: about 130 litres of mostly rain water per cup.
Moderate coffee drinking is linked to lower risk of several diseases.
Sun-grown coffee replaces forest. Shade-grown coffee can shelter birds almost as well as forest.
Most of the world's 12 million coffee farms are smallholders, and many earn below the poverty line.
stages: Brewing|2|Boiling more water than you need
Milk|2|Often more carbon than the coffee
deps: A narrow band of mountains|Arabica only thrives at mild temperatures. About half of today's coffee land could be unsuitable by 2050.
Smallholder farmers|Their average age is rising and their children are leaving the trade.
alts: Fairtrade or Rainforest Alliance beans|Minimum prices for farmers and rules that protect forest.|-1.5,-2,1,-1,0|EASY|0|0
Oat milk instead of dairy|Roughly a third of the carbon of cow's milk.|-1,-2,1,-1.5,-2.5|EASY|40|9000
Bring a reusable cup|Around 500 billion disposable cups are used each year.|-1.5,-2,1,-1.5,-2.5|EASY|5|0
qa: Does the cup or the coffee matter more?|The coffee, then the milk. The disposable cup is a small share of the carbon, though a large share of the litter.
Will climate change take away coffee?|Not entirely, but it will move and cost more. Wild Arabica is already listed as endangered.

name: Cup of tea
headline: Most of this cup's carbon comes from the kettle, not the tea: boiling only what you need can halve it.
why: A black tea is around 20 g CO₂e; most of that is boiling the water.
About 30 litres per cup to grow the leaves, mostly rain.
Unsweetened tea is linked to better heart health.
Tea estates replace forest on hillsides but keep soil covered all year.
Tea pickers on many estates earn very low wages and depend on the estate for housing.
deps: Hand labour|Almost all quality tea is still picked by hand.
Monsoon rain|Tea yields track rainfall closely.
alts: Boil only the water you need|The easiest carbon saving in the kitchen.|-0.5,-1.5,1.5,-1,-2.5|EASY|15|0
Loose-leaf, fairly traded tea|No plastic bag, better pay for pickers.|-1,-1.5,1.5,-0.5,-0.5|EASY|0|0
qa: Is tea better than coffee?|Per cup, yes: roughly a quarter of the water and less carbon. Add a lot of milk to either and the milk dominates.
src: Oxfam, Addressing the Human Cost of Assam Tea

name: Fresh fruit
headline: A banana travels thousands of kilometres by ship and still has a smaller footprint than almost anything else you could snack on.
why: Grown in sunlight, shipped by sea, wrapped by nature. Around 0.1 kg CO₂e each.
Around 100–160 litres per piece, mostly rain.
Fruit is one of the clearest wins in nutrition science.
Monoculture plantations use heavy pesticides; orchards can be good wildlife habitat.
Plantation workers face low pay and pesticide exposure; fair-trade fruit pays better.
stages: Waste|2|A third of fruit is never eaten
deps: Pollinators|Most fruit needs insects to set.
One fragile variety|Nearly all export bananas are genetically identical Cavendish clones, and a fungus is spreading through them.
alts: Local fruit in season|Avoids heated greenhouses and air freight.|-0.5,-1.5,4,0,0|EASY|5|0
Eat it before it browns|Wasted food is the footprint with no benefit.|-0.5,-1.5,4,-1,-1|EASY|10|3000
qa: Does air-freighted fruit matter?|Yes. Berries, asparagus or mangoes flown in can have ten times the footprint of the same food shipped by sea. If it is highly perishable and from far away, it probably flew.

name: Vegetables
headline: If everyone ate like this plate, the world would need about a quarter of today's farmland.
why: Among the lowest-carbon foods: usually under 1 kg CO₂e per kilo.
About 300 litres per kilo, a fiftieth of beef.
The best-evidenced food group for long-term health.
Low land use. Organic and mixed farms support far more insects and birds.
Field harvest work is seasonal and often underpaid.
stages: Waste|2|Vegetables are the most thrown-away food at home
deps: Living soil|A handful holds more organisms than there are people on Earth.
Seasonal workers|Much of the harvest still depends on migrant labour.
alts: Seasonal and field-grown|A winter tomato from a heated greenhouse can emit ten times more than a summer one.|0,-1,5,0,0|EASY|10|0
Grow some yourself|Herbs and salad on a windowsill: zero packaging, zero transport.|0,-0.5,5,0.5,1|MEDIUM|5|0
qa: Is local always better?|No. How food is grown matters more than how far it travels. Transport is typically under a tenth of a food's footprint, unless it flew.

name: Bread
headline: Bread is one of the most wasted foods on Earth: in the UK alone, around 20 million slices are binned every day.
why: About 1 kg CO₂e per loaf. Nearly half comes from the fertiliser used to grow the wheat.
About 1,600 litres per kilo of bread.
Wholegrain bread is good for you; white bread less so.
Wheat monocultures and fertiliser run-off, though far less land than animal foods.
A staple that feeds billions affordably.
deps: Nitrogen fertiliser|Made from natural gas. It feeds about half of humanity and pollutes rivers.
A few breadbasket regions|A drought or war in one of them moves bread prices worldwide.
alts: Freeze what you won't eat|Toast from frozen. Ends most bread waste.|-1.5,-2.5,1,-1,0|EASY|10|15000
Wholegrain from a local bakery|More fibre, less packaging.|-2,-3,2,-1,1|EASY|0|0
qa: Why is fertiliser such a big deal?|Making it burns gas, and once on the field some turns into nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas about 270 times stronger than CO₂.

name: Pizza
headline: About half of this pizza's footprint is the cheese. Swap the toppings and you change the planet's bill more than the base ever could.
why: Cheese is carbon-heavy; pepperoni or beef adds more.
Around 1,260 litres for a margherita.
Fine as a meal; salty and calorie-dense as a habit.
Dairy needs pasture and feed land.
One of the world's great shared foods.
deps: Dairy herds|It takes about 10 litres of milk to make a kilo of cheese.
Processing tomatoes|Often grown in water-stressed regions.
alts: Vegetable toppings, lighter on cheese|Cuts the footprint by about a third.|-2,-2.5,0.5,-1.5,0.5|EASY|20|10000
Share one, add a salad|Less food waste and a better meal.|-2,-2.5,1,-1.5,1|EASY|15|8000
qa: Is delivery worse than cooking?|The delivery trip is usually small next to the ingredients. What is on the pizza matters far more than how it arrives.

name: Cheese & dairy
unit: 100 g of cheese (or about a litre of milk)
headline: It takes around ten litres of milk to make one kilo of cheese, which is why cheese has a bigger carbon footprint than chicken or pork.
why: Cows emit methane whether they are raised for beef or milk.
Around 1,000 litres per litre of milk, mainly for feed.
Good source of calcium and protein; high in saturated fat.
Dairy uses a lot of pasture and feed land, and slurry pollutes rivers.
Dairy farmers are squeezed by low prices; many small farms have closed.
deps: Grass and feed|A dairy cow eats over 20 kg of dry feed a day.
Clean rivers|Slurry and fertiliser run-off are leading causes of river pollution in dairy regions.
alts: Oat or soy drink|About a third of the carbon and a tenth of the land of cow's milk.|-1,-1.5,0.5,-0.5,0|EASY|80|60000
Less, better cheese|Buy the good one and use half as much.|-2,-2,0.5,-2.5,0|EASY|40|20000
qa: Which plant milk is best?|Oat and soy are consistently low on carbon, water and land. Almond is low-carbon but thirsty. All of them beat dairy on every environmental measure.

name: Chocolate
headline: About 1.5 million children work growing cocoa in West Africa, where most of the world's chocolate begins.
why: Cocoa grown on freshly cleared forest carries a large carbon debt.
Around 17,000 litres per kilo of chocolate, mostly rain on cocoa trees.
Dark chocolate in small amounts is fine; most bars are mainly sugar.
Côte d'Ivoire has lost most of its forest, largely to cocoa.
Most cocoa farmers earn under a dollar a day. Hazardous child labour is widespread.
deps: Rainforest climate|Cocoa grows only within about 20° of the equator.
Two countries|Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana grow around 60% of the world's cocoa.
Tiny midges|Cocoa flowers are pollinated almost only by a midge the size of a pinhead.
alts: Fairtrade or bean-to-bar chocolate|Higher, more traceable payments to farmers.|-2.5,-3,-1,-2.5,-1|EASY|0|0
Darker, smaller, slower|Less sugar and milk; you tend to eat less of it.|-2,-2.5,0,-3,-3|EASY|5|5000
qa: Do certification labels actually work?|They help, but not enough on their own. Certified farmers earn more and use fewer hazardous practices, yet child labour is still found on certified farms. Brands that publish exactly which farms they buy from are a stronger signal.
Why is cocoa so tied to poverty?|Farmers receive about 6% of the price of a chocolate bar. Most of the value is added after the beans leave the country.

name: Eggs
headline: An egg takes about 200 litres of water to produce, almost all of it to grow the hen's feed.
why: About 0.3 kg CO₂e per egg: one of the lowest-carbon animal proteins.
About 200 litres per egg.
Dense, complete protein.
Feed crops and manure; far less land than meat.
Caged systems are still the norm in much of the world.
deps: Grain and soy|A hen eats about 2 kg of feed per kilo of eggs.
alts: Free-range or organic eggs|Better lives for hens.|-1.5,-2.5,1.5,-1,0.5|EASY|0|0
Scrambled tofu or chickpea omelette|Lower on every environmental axis.|-1,-1.5,1.5,-0.5,0|MEDIUM|15|15000
qa: Are eggs a good swap for meat?|Environmentally, yes: roughly a tenth of beef's carbon per gram of protein.

name: Beer, wine & spirits
unit: one drink (a glass of wine or a half-litre of beer)
headline: For wine, the heaviest part of the footprint is often the glass bottle, not the grapes.
why: Around 0.3–0.5 kg CO₂e a drink; glass bottles and refrigeration dominate.
About 110 litres for a glass of wine, 150 for a half-litre of beer.
The World Health Organization says no level of drinking is safe for health; alcohol causes about 2.6 million deaths a year.
Vineyards and barley fields are monocultures, often heavily sprayed.
Central to social life in many cultures, and a major cause of violence and accidents.
deps: Glass furnaces|They run at about 1,500 °C around the clock.
Climate-sensitive grapes|Wine regions are already shifting towards the poles.
alts: Draught, can or refill|Lighter packaging, lower footprint than single-use glass.|-1,-2,-3,-1,-1|EASY|10|0
Alcohol-free version|Same ritual, without the health cost.|-1.5,-2,0,-1,0|EASY|0|0
qa: Is a can really better than a bottle?|Usually. A can is far lighter to ship and is recycled much more often and more efficiently than glass.
src: WHO Global Status Report on Alcohol and Health 2024

name: Soft drink
unit: one 330 ml can of sugary drink
headline: Recycling this can saves 95% of the energy needed to make a new one, and it can be back on the shelf in about 60 days.
why: Around 0.2–0.3 kg CO₂e, largely the aluminium can.
Around 170–300 litres, mostly to grow the sugar.
Sugary drinks are a leading driver of obesity, type 2 diabetes and tooth decay.
Sugar cane and bauxite mining both clear land.
Bottling plants have been accused of draining local groundwater in water-stressed places.
stages: After use|1|Recycle it: it never wears out
deps: Cheap electricity|Aluminium smelting is so energy-hungry it is nicknamed solid electricity.
Local groundwater|A bottling plant draws from the same aquifer as its neighbours.
alts: Tap water, sparkling if you like|No sugar, no can, about a thousandth of the footprint.|0,0,3,0,0|EASY|40|40000
Always recycle the can|Aluminium recycles forever. About 75% of all aluminium ever made is still in use.|-1,-2.5,-3,-1,-1|EASY|10|0
qa: Is diet soda the answer?|It removes the sugar and most of the water footprint. The can and the chilled supply chain stay the same.

name: Plastic water bottle
unit: one 500 ml single-use plastic bottle of water
headline: People buy about a million plastic bottles every minute. A litre of bottled water can contain around 240,000 tiny plastic particles.
why: About 80 g CO₂e each: hundreds of times more than the same water from a tap.
It takes roughly 1.5–3 litres of water to deliver one litre in a bottle.
The water is safe, but studies now find hundreds of thousands of nanoplastic particles per litre; long-term effects are still unknown.
Bottles are among the most common items in ocean and river litter and take centuries to break down.
Bottling can compete with communities for groundwater. In places without safe tap water, bottles are a lifeline.
stages: Afterlife|3|Fewer than a third are recycled worldwide
deps: Fossil fuels|Almost all plastic is made from oil and gas.
Waste systems|Where collection is weak, bottles end up in rivers.
alts: Refillable bottle + tap water|Pays back its footprint in a few dozen refills.|0,0,1,0,0|EASY|30|500
Filter jug if you dislike the taste|Solves the usual reason people buy bottled.|0,0,1,0,0|EASY|30|500
qa: Isn't the bottle recyclable?|Yes, and it should be recycled. But worldwide only a minority of bottles are collected, and most of those are turned into fibre rather than new bottles, so the loop is not closed.
Are microplastics harmful?|We don't know yet. They are found in blood, lungs and placentas. Research on health effects is early and the honest answer is uncertain.

name: Mixed meal
headline: Food causes about a quarter of all greenhouse gas emissions, and a third of all food is never eaten.
why: A typical meal is 1–3 kg CO₂e. Whether it contains beef or lamb changes it more than anything else.
Farming uses about 70% of all the freshwater people withdraw.
Depends on what is on the plate; point the camera closer for a better answer.
Farming is the main cause of wildlife loss worldwide.
Farm and kitchen work is often low paid; food is also how people come together.
stages: Farming|3|Where most of the footprint is
deps: Topsoil|It takes centuries to form a few centimetres.
Pollinators|Three-quarters of food crops benefit from them.
Fresh water|Seven-tenths of withdrawals go to farms.
alts: Make plants the main event|Shifting from a meat-heavy to a plant-rich diet can halve your food footprint.|-1,-2,3,-1,0|MEDIUM|500|200000
Cook what you'll eat, eat what you cooked|Cutting food waste is the cheapest climate action there is.|-1.5,-2.5,1,-2,0|EASY|150|50000
qa: What is the single most effective food change?|Eating less beef and lamb. They provide a small share of calories and a large share of food's emissions and land use.
